newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar falls below 111.60 yen, lowest since Nov 25.
newsitem.headline: Dollar falls below 111.60 yen, lowest since Nov 25.

text.p: The dollar fell below 111.60 yen on Wednesday morning, its lowest level since November 25, 1996, dealers said.

Dealers said Japan's April current account data released this morning, which showed a 92.7 percent rise in the surplus from the previous year, was no longer a factor in influencing the dollar/yen rate, but long-term concerns over Japan's trade surplus remained.
Japan's current account surplus increased to 1.09 trillion yen in April, which was mostly within market expectations, dealers said. The surplus stood at 566.66 yen a year earlier.
U.S. funds were behind the latest dollar sales, market sources said, while a trust bank dealer said Japanese investors began selling dollars for hedge purposes when the greenback began falling.
Dealers said the market is intent on testing the dollar's downside.
